newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ short end closes stable despite softer TWI.
newsitem.headline: NZ short end closes stable despite softer TWI.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (JUN) 92.85 (PREV 92.84) 90-DAYS 7.02 (PREV 7.02)
OVERNIGHT CASH 6.40 PCT (PREV 6.50) US 5-YR 6.56 (PREV 6.50)
* NZ money mkt, shorter end of bond curve finishes steady
* Long bonds remain vulnerable to weaker U.S.
* Dealers see scope for further slight easing in conditions
The short end of New Zealand's yield curve ended flat on Wednesday despite a softer currency Trade-Weighted Index.
After opening higher at 7.05 percent, the 90-days managed to rally back down to end at Tuesday's closing level of 7.02 percent, despite a further softening in the TWI during the session.
The TWI ended at 67.83, down from its 67.91 open and 68.06 finish on Tuesday.
"There's nothing friendly in the other markets, but the short end has been quite resilient really," one dealer said.

Domestic trading banks had bought bills in early trade, absorbing selling pressure and keeping the money market reasonably firm. Recent Eurokiwi issuance and a higher overnight cash rate were also helping to add value to the local market.
The 02/00 maturity ended flat at 7.37 percent but the long bond remained subject to global weakness and sold off four basis points to 7.60 percent on the back of U.S. Treasury selling.
Dealers said the overall tone was mixed, but fears were fading about the prospects of a sell-off in the currency and there was scope for the 90-days to rally back below seven percent.

"I think the market would be nervous about easing a lot further. You might get another 10, 20 basis points easier, but I doubt we're going to get to where we were the other day, before the Reserve Bank made its statement," a dealer said.
The 90-day bill rates were down at 6.90 percent and the TWI at 67.65 when the RBNZ said on Monday conditions were settling too far from desired levels and it wanted them firmer.

The market continues to look for a clarification of desired monetary conditions from the RBNZ and its June monetary policy statement. During the day the RBNZ said the report would be delivered on June 27.
-- Catherine McCaw, Wellington newsroom (64 4) 471 4275
